title: Arabic groups words into three parts of speech
rule: Use the Arabic categories: اِسْمٌ، فِعْلٌ، حَرْفٌ.

title: Sun letters borrow the lām sound
rule: Keep الـ in writing; double the sun letter in speech.
note: The ل stays in writing but is not heard. The sun letter doubles.

title: Moon letters let the lām be heard
rule: With a moon letter, keep the “l” sound of al.
note: A moon letter keeps the l sound of al.

title: Let words flow into الـ
rule: The spelling stays; the opening vowel joins smoothly to the previous word.
note: The alif stays in writing; in speech the opening vowel drops.

title: A shorter vowel when فِي meets الـ
rule: Write فِي الْبَيْتِ; connect it in speech as “fil-bayti.”
note: The long vowel of فِي shortens before الـ.

title: A connecting vowel beyond الـ
rule: Hamzat al-wasl drops in connected speech in اِسْمٌ and اِبْنٌ too.
note: Hamzat al-wasl drops after another word.

title: A final ى can sound like alif
rule: Read the final dotless ى in this word as a long “ā.”
note: Dotless final ى is read as a long ā.

title: When لِـ meets الـ, drop the alif
rule: لِـ + الـ becomes لِلـ in writing, and the noun is majrur.
note: No extra alif is written: لِلْ, never لِالْ.

title: A short “i” connects ذَهَبَتْ to الـ
rule: Before الـ, connect ذَهَبَتْ with a short “i”: ذَهَبَتِ الْبِنْتُ.
note: A short i joins the verb to الـ.

title: An extra alif with this “an” ending
rule: Write كِتَابًا with ا; write سَيَّارَةً without an extra ا.
note: The extra alif goes on كِتَابًا, but not after ة.

title: “Son of” between two names has a special spelling
rule: In بِلَالُ بْنُ حَامِدٍ, write بْنُ and omit Bilal’s tanwin.
note: Write بْنُ; Bilal has no tanwin.

title: Tanwin gets a linking “i” before hamzat al-wasl
rule: A linking sound can change pronunciation without changing grammatical case.
note: A linking i follows tanwin before wasl.

title: A linking “u” follows these final مْ forms
rule: Before wasl here, connect the final مْ with “u.”
note: A linking u follows these final مْ forms.

title: Questioning مَا loses its alif after a preposition
rule: Drop the alif of questioning مَا after these prepositions.
note: Questioning مَا loses its alif after a preposition.

title: Question أَ becomes a long آ before الـ here
rule: Question أَ directly before الـ is written and read differently from أَهَذَا.
note: Question أَ becomes آ only right before الـ.

title: A final ى changes spelling before an attached pronoun
rule: Before these attached pronouns, final long-ā ى is written ا.
note: Final ى is written ا before an attached pronoun.

title: Why “I eat” begins with آ
rule: Write آكُلُ, آخُذُ and آمُرُ with the long opening آ.
note: Two hamzas merge into a long ā.

title: The silent waw in عَمْرٌو
rule: Write the silent waw in عَمْرٌو, but omit it in عَمْرًا.
note: The silent waw is written in عَمْرٌو only.

title: Write ibn between names with care
rule: The spelling depends on both the name construction and the written line.
note: Alif is omitted only with no title and one written line.

title: Question hamza replaces wasl hamza
rule: The remaining hamza asks the question; it is not the original wasl.
note: The question hamza replaces the wasl hamza.

title: Form VIII drops wasl after question hamza too
rule: Do not add a second helping hamza after the question.
note: No second helping hamza after the question.
